issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting guidance about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: it first instructs that the stock should be a final (instance) field initialized in the SealSaloon constructor, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is inconsistent and will confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a class-level static field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: decide whether stock is a per-instance final field or a shared static field. If stock should be shared across all SealSaloon instances, state that stock must be declared static final and initialized in a static initializer or inline (as shown in the solution). If stock should be per-instance, remove the requirement that stock be static. Update the problem statement to remove the instruction to initialize stock in the instance constructor when it is required to be static.
